authentication: none for the tenant endpoints a public careers site itself calls; there is no vendor-neutral or authenticated API in scope
free_tier: free web access to employer career sites; the vendors' own products are commercial
rate_limits: UNKNOWN - no published limit; each employer tenant enforces its own
licence: employer career-site content; no open licence. redistribution_allowed recorded as NO for structured reuse.
entity_identifiers: Workday CXS: tenant name + site name + job requisition id (tenant-scoped)
job title / location strings only for cross-employer work
timestamp_fields: Workday CXS: postedOn (relative text such as 'Posted Today' in some tenants; exact timestamps vary by tenant)
no stable cross-employer publication field was observed
known_limitations: There is no vendor-neutral API: each employer runs its own tenant (Workday: <tenant>.wdN.myworkdayjobs.com/wday/cxs/...) or its own hosted careers product (Phenom), so any connector is per-employer and cannot be generalised.
The Workday CXS guesses tested (philips/wd3, gehc/wd5) both returned HTTP 404 JSON: the tenant+site pair must be discovered per employer and guessing is not a viable strategy.

The historical Phenom host jobs.medtronic.com resolves but presents a TLS certificate whose name does not match the host. A compliant client must not disable verification, so that host was recorded as unfetchable rather than worked around.

Public careers pages are client-rendered: the Philips search-results page returns HTML with no job records in it, so parsing requires either a JS runtime (out of scope) or the tenant JSON endpoint behind it.
Undocumented internal endpoints can change without notice; anything built on them is a maintenance liability and must be treated as best-effort.
No department taxonomy is portable; role classification would again be a title-text heuristic.
research_value: Documents why the five firms' hiring data is hard to get: they appear to run bespoke employer career stacks (Phenom/Workday-style) rather than a generic job board. This is the negative evidence that justifies either per-employer adapters (high maintenance, per-firm legal review) or dropping hiring volume as a MedRadar signal for these five firms.
cost_notes: free for the public tenant endpoints; commercial for the vendors' own products
